edits.old:
- **Foot construction and bedding (r7).** Each foot is a PA66 or PBT block of height h_f = 2.54 mm - t_bed = 2.24 mm at
  t_bed 0.30 mm (bed range 0.15-0.45 mm). It is bonded to the CR underside with neutral-cure RTV silicone before seating. The
  header bodies set the CR height, so the feet take no preload, and no wet adhesive is present while the 22 MB joints are
  soldered. After those joints are soldered and inspected, a neutral-cure RTV bed fills the 0.30 +- 0.15 mm gap between each
  foot and the polyimide sheet.
edits.new:
- **Foot construction and bedding (r7).** Each foot is a PA66 or PBT block of height h_f = 2.54 mm - t_bed - t_bond = 2.19 mm
  at t_bed 0.30 mm and t_bond 0.05 mm (block tolerance +0/-0.05 mm). The CR-side bond is a 0.05 mm acrylic transfer tape
  (TODO(verify: tape datasheet, temperature rating)). (**superseded in r7:** h_f = 2.54 mm - t_bed = 2.24 mm with an RTV bond
  of unstated thickness, cured before seating.) The header bodies and the feet both stand on the sheet, so t_bed does not
  depend on the MB, CR or sheet thickness. The tape bonds each foot before seating, the header bodies set the CR height, and
  no wet adhesive is present while the 22 MB joints are soldered.

  The tolerance budget of t_bed (H.23(i)) has four contributors: the header body +-0.13 mm (TODO(verify: Samtec TSW
  drawing)), the CR local bow (IPC-6012 0.75 % of the lever: +-0.118 mm at FT1, +-0.066 mm at FT2), the block
  +0/-0.05 mm and the tape 0-0.05 mm. The nominal bed is 0.300 mm and the mean is 0.350 mm. The worst case is
  0.052-0.648 mm at FT1 and 0.104-0.596 mm at FT2; the RSS bands are 0.171-0.529 mm and 0.200-0.500 mm. The worst case
  therefore falls outside the 0.15-0.45 mm bed range on both sides. A foot that is too tall becomes a hard prop and
  preloads the joints; a foot that is too short leaves a bed thicker than the stiffness range of H.23(i).

  The measured gate PM4 (2d) dry-seats the CR on the sheet after the feet are taped and before the 22 joints are
  soldered. A 0.05 mm feeler must not enter under any header body; at each foot a 0.15 mm feeler must enter and a
  0.45 mm feeler must not. A Monte-Carlo estimate with uniform contributors (ORDER OF MAGNITUDE) passes 79.7 % of FT1
  builds (2.2 % too tall, 18.1 % too short) and 85.8 % of FT2 builds (0.2 % and 14.0 %). A rejected foot is re-made.
  The 0.15-0.45 mm bed range is therefore a gated range, and "the feet take no preload" holds for a build that passes (2d).

  As the placement aid, the CR bottom silkscreen carries the outline of each foot body, a long-axis tick on FT1 (long axis
  along x) and a ring around the FT2 fill hole (A.8). FT2 is square, so the outline also sets its orientation. A pin of
  0.9-1.0 mm through the CR fill hole and the foot hole locates FT2. PM4 (2c) measures the three edge distances that the
  A.7 placement tolerance bounds (FT1 0.294 / 0.304 mm, FT2 0.250 mm).

  After the 22 MB joints are soldered and inspected, a flowable alkoxy-cure silicone RTV bed fills the gap between each foot
  and the polyimide sheet (nominal 0.30 mm, gated 0.15-0.45 mm).

edits.old:
- **Tab stiffness and pin loads (r7, H.23(i); ORDER OF MAGNITUDE).** These figures assume a 20 GPa laminate, a clamped root and
  an RTV modulus of 1-3 MPa (ASSUMPTION, TODO(verify: RTV datasheet)); every resonance figure is an upper estimate, and MS5, MS6
  and T-F-18 decide. Tab X has a tip stiffness of 35.8 N/mm and 63.2 N/mm at the foot, against an RTV bed of 14-128 N/mm; its
  first mode is 1664-2353 Hz unpropped and 1924-3336 Hz propped (bed E 1-3 MPa, t 0.30 mm). Tab Y has 266.3 / 603.8 N/mm against
  a bed of 36-320 N/mm; its first mode is 4531-6407 Hz unpropped and 4726-7204 Hz propped. The worst header-pin load at 30 g is
  0.208-0.322 N without the feet and 0.168-0.297 N with them (r6 CR alone 0.067-0.134 N). A 10 N push at the tab X tip loads
  the worst pin with 2.69 N without FT1 and 0.52-1.99 N with it; at the tab Y tip the figures are 3.06 N and 1.64-2.83 N.
edits.new:
- **Tab stiffness and pin loads (r7, H.23(i); ORDER OF MAGNITUDE).** These figures assume a 20 GPa laminate, a clamped root and
  an RTV modulus of 1-3 MPa (ASSUMPTION, TODO(verify: RTV datasheet)); MS5, MS6 and T-F-18 decide. The unpropped resonance
  figures are upper estimates (clamped root). For tab Y the clamp along the pin-11 row y 64.484 is held by pin 11 alone within
  the tab width, so the tab Y figures are the least conservative. Tab X has a tip stiffness of 35.8 N/mm and 63.2 N/mm at the
  foot, against an RTV bed of 14-128 N/mm; its first mode is 1664-2353 Hz unpropped. Tab Y has 266.3 / 603.8 N/mm against a
  bed of 36-320 N/mm; its first mode is 4531-6407 Hz unpropped. The propped first modes are neither upper nor lower bounds.
  With k_s = E A / t (t_bed 0.30 mm) they are 1924-3336 Hz (tab X) and 4726-7204 Hz (tab Y). The bonded-thin-layer (Gent)
  factor 1 + 2S^2 raises k_s up to x8 at FT1 (S 1.90) and x23 at FT2 (S 3.33); with it the propped first modes are
  3235-7190 Hz (tab X) and 7905-17112 Hz (tab Y). (**superseded in r7:** "every resonance figure is an upper estimate".)
  The MS5 comparison uses the lowest unpropped figure, tab X 1664 Hz. The worst header-pin load at 30 g is 0.208-0.322 N
  without the feet and 0.168-0.297 N with them (r6 CR alone 0.067-0.134 N). The with-feet pin loads are upper estimates on
  the bed axis, because a stiffer (confined) bed unloads the pins. A 10 N push at the tab X tip loads the worst pin with
  2.69 N without FT1 and 0.52-1.99 N with it. At the tab Y tip (28.00, 76.00) the figures are 3.05 N and 1.63-2.82 N
  (**superseded in r7:** 3.06 N and 1.64-2.83 N).
- **Feet effect and the fitting decision (r7, H.23(i); ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, bed confinement not modelled).** The feet are
  fitted by default by operator ruling. Their effect on the distributed load is small: at 30 g they cut the worst-pin load
  by 7-21 %. Their effect on a tip push is larger. FT1 takes 2.41-8.79 N of a 10 N tab X tip push and cuts the worst-pin
  load by 26-81 %. FT1 also props the softer tab (35.8 N/mm), whose unpropped first mode 1664-2353 Hz lies inside the MS5
  band of 0.1-8 kHz. FT2 takes 0.82-5.09 N of a 10 N tab Y tip push and cuts the worst-pin load by 7-47 %. Tab Y is stiff
  (266.3 N/mm, unpropped first mode 4531-6407 Hz). FT2 is therefore kept as a margin against handling loads at the tab Y
  far edge until MS5 and T-F-18 report. When the MS5 spectrum shows no MB excitation above the logger noise floor within
  2.3-8 kHz (0.5-2 times the tab Y unpropped band, clipped at 8 kHz), FT2 may be omitted by operator ruling. Its
  footprint, keep-out and fill hole then stay on the CR.
